answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents route transactions through a cryptographic inlet where entering the network requires staking tokens. To scale verification, the network illuminates fraudulent clusters like a lantern by enforcing quadratic stake burning: registering n identities scales the slashed cost superlinearly as O(n^2). This economic friction anchors agent identity to immutable shale strata, rendering large-scale Sybil attacks mathematically non-viable through superlinear cost scaling.
